name: Botshido
author: AlgeniaLab

sections.description:
Most chatbots just answer. Botshido answers from your own content, in a voice that sounds like your brand, and points visitors to the right next step. And it is built to be used responsibly: consent first, your data in your own database, and privacy tools included.

Visitors ask a question in a chat widget and get an answer based on your content (your pages and posts, FAQs, and the text and documents you add) and your instructions, not generic internet knowledge. You connect your own account with OpenAI, Mistral AI, Anthropic (Claude) or xAI (Grok), tell the chatbot who it is and what it knows, and place it on your site. There are no message limits in the plugin and no markup on AI costs: you pay your provider directly, at their prices.

Documentation: Setup wizard and first chatbot · Get an API key and understand costs · Privacy and the EU AI Act · All documentation (also in Italian).

Why Botshido

1. Your content. Your knowledge. Better answers.

Build the knowledge base from your posts and pages, FAQ pairs, and training text or files (.txt and .md); Botshido Pro can also import external web pages. For each question Botshido finds the relevant excerpts and answers from them. Tell it what to say when it does not know, to reduce made-up answers.

2. A character, not a generic widget.

Give your chatbot a personality: a name, your own avatar and chat button icon, a tone of voice (from serious to funny, from formal to casual), colors, fonts and an opening line, with a live preview while you work. You can even add a large side avatar that stands next to the chat window. Start from one of three bundled characters (Ninji, Leo or Aria), or import a template file (ZIP, with its images), and make it sound like your brand, not like a manual.

3. It guides, it does not just reply.

Quick-question buttons and content blocks show the right link, button or card at the right moment: when a visitor mentions a keyword, or after a number of messages. A question about opening hours can end with a “Book now” button instead of a paragraph. (Botshido Pro adds fully guided conversations with branches, lead collection and human handoff.)

4. GDPR-friendly by design.

Botshido gives you the tools to run a chatbot responsibly:

  • Consent before anything happens. Turn on the consent notice and the chat does not start until the visitor accepts. This is enforced on the server: no message is sent to the AI provider, and no analytics event is recorded, without consent. Visitors can also decline.
  • Your texts, your policy. Edit the notice, the accept and decline buttons, and link your own privacy policy.
  • Your data stays on your site. Conversations and analytics are stored in your own WordPress database, not on our servers.
  • You decide how long to keep it. Set automatic retention for conversations and analytics: older records are deleted for you.
  • Data minimization. Analytics store a minimized page address: tracking parameters and personal query strings are dropped.
  • WordPress privacy tools. Conversations and analytics events are included in the WordPress personal data export and erase requests.
  • Clean uninstall. Deleting the plugin removes its tables and settings.

Compliance also depends on your privacy policy and on your agreement with the AI provider, so this is not legal advice.

AI transparency. Botshido helps you tell visitors that they are talking to an AI, as the EU AI Act (Art. 50) asks of chatbots: the bundled chatbots open with a greeting that says so, the admin suggests a bot name that leaves no doubt, an AI Disclaimer link in the chat footer explains it in full (translatable per chatbot with WPML or Polylang), and the assistant is instructed to say it is an AI whenever it is asked. How you word and configure it remains your responsibility. Free checklist and privacy notice template.

5. Your costs stay under your control.

Bring your own key. There is no per-message fee from us and no markup. Switch provider or model whenever you want. Built-in per-visitor rate limits and a daily cap on AI requests (adjustable by developers with a filter) help protect your API bill from runaway usage and abuse.

6. See what works.

Built-in analytics show how many visitors saw the widget, opened the chat and started a conversation, so you can tune your opening line and your content. Conversations are saved in your WordPress admin, so you can read what people really ask.

7. Easy to set up.

A setup wizard walks you through the key, the model and your first content. Place the chatbot as a floating widget on the whole site, only on selected pages, or anywhere with the [botshido] shortcode. It is multilingual-ready, with WPML and Polylang integration, and answers in the language the visitor writes in (quality depends on the model).

Everything in the free plugin

  • One chatbot with its own prompts, provider, model, tone and appearance
  • Four providers, all included: OpenAI, Mistral AI, Anthropic (Claude) and xAI (Grok)
  • Knowledge base from posts and pages, FAQ pairs and training text or files, with keyword search
  • Floating widget or [botshido] shortcode, with page-level display rules
  • Quick questions and content blocks with keyword and message-count triggers
  • Your own avatars and icons (chatbot, visitor, chat button and a large side avatar), colors, fonts, texts and live preview; three bundled templates and ZIP template import with one-step undo
  • Analytics, conversation history, setup wizard
  • GDPR tools: consent notice, retention, privacy export and erase

Pro features

Botshido Pro is a separate paid license, bought on botshido.com. The code for these features is not part of this plugin:

  • Unlimited chatbots and a public chatbot switcher
  • Guided conversational flows, lead collection and advanced triggers
  • Human handoff with availability hours and operator notifications
  • Embedding-based (semantic) retrieval and URL import for the knowledge base
  • A/B testing of opening messages and analytics CSV export
  • WooCommerce integration
  • Online template library, template export and creation of chatbots from templates

API keys

You need an API key from at least one supported provider. Keys can be stored in the plugin settings or defined as PHP constants (NINJAIBOT_OPENAI_API_KEY, NINJAIBOT_MISTRAL_API_KEY, NINJAIBOT_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, NINJAIBOT_GROK_API_KEY) in wp-config.php.

External services

This plugin connects to third-party AI services to generate chat responses and (optionally) text embeddings for the knowledge base. Requests are only sent to the provider you configure, and only when a visitor uses the chat (or when the knowledge base is indexed with embeddings enabled).

What is sent: the visitor’s chat messages, the conversation context, your configured prompts, and relevant excerpts of your indexed site content. Your API key is sent to authenticate each request.

  • OpenAI (api.openai.com) — chat responses and embeddings. Terms of use, Privacy policy
  • Mistral AI (api.mistral.ai) — chat responses and embeddings. Terms of service, Privacy policy
  • Anthropic (api.anthropic.com) — chat responses. Terms of service, Privacy policy
  • xAI (api.x.ai) — chat responses. Terms of service, Privacy policy

Additionally, if you configure lead-collection webhooks or index external URLs into the knowledge base, the plugin sends requests to the hosts you explicitly allow via the ninjaibot_allowed_webhook_hosts filter. The Pro version can also download chatbot templates, with their images, from botshido.com; this feature is not part of this free plugin.

Freemius (api.freemius.com, wp.freemius.com) — this plugin uses the Freemius SDK for licensing, updates and optional usage insights. Nothing is sent until an administrator opts in on the activation screen (it can be skipped). After opting in, Freemius receives the site URL, WordPress and PHP versions, the plugin version and the administrator’s name and email address; it never receives chatbot conversations, your content or API keys. Terms of service, Privacy policy

Source code and third-party libraries

All JavaScript and CSS written for this plugin is shipped as editable source (assets/admin/, assets/public/, assets/js/, assets/css/ and inline code in the PHP templates). There is no build or compilation step. In particular, assets/admin/js/ninjaibot-flow-editor.js is the original, formatted source of the flow editor; there is no separate generated version. A JavaScript formatter is optional and is not needed to run or rebuild the plugin.

Bundled third-party libraries:

  • marked 18.1.3 (MIT) — assets/public/js/marked.umd.js, the unmodified UMD build from https://github.com/markedjs/marked
  • DOMPurify 3.4.8 (Apache-2.0 / MPL-2.0) — assets/public/js/purify.min.js, the unmodified official release build; source at https://github.com/cure53/DOMPurify
  • Freemius SDK (GPLv2+) — vendor/freemius/, https://github.com/Freemius/wordpress-sdk
sections.installation:
1. Upload the botshido folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin. Activation creates the required database tables.
  3. Go to Botshido → Settings and add the API key for your chosen LLM provider.
  4. Enable the widget, or place the [botshido] shortcode in a post or page.
  5. Read the documentation at https://botshido.com/docs/ (Italian: https://botshido.com/docs/it/); it is also linked from the Plugins screen and the Botshido menu.
sections.faq:
Do I need an API key?

Yes. The plugin does not ship with any AI service; you connect your own account with OpenAI, Mistral AI, Anthropic (Claude) or xAI (Grok). Usage is billed by the provider according to your plan with them. Create the key in your provider’s dashboard and paste it in Botshido → Settings. Step by step, and what you pay for: https://botshido.com/docs/start/api-keys-costs/

Can I use it with ChatGPT?

Botshido works with OpenAI’s models, the same family behind ChatGPT, through your own OpenAI API key. A ChatGPT subscription is a different product and does not include an API key: you create the key in the OpenAI developer dashboard and pay for what your visitors use.

Does it work with Claude and Grok?

Yes. All four providers (OpenAI, Mistral AI, Anthropic Claude and xAI Grok) are included in the free plugin. You pick one per chatbot and can change it at any time.

Is the free plugin limited?

The free plugin runs one chatbot, with no limit on messages. Everything listed under “Free features” is included. The Pro features listed above are sold separately.

How does the chatbot know about my business?

You choose what goes into the knowledge base: your posts and pages, FAQ pairs, and training text or files (.txt and .md). Botshido Pro can also import external web pages, so the knowledge is not limited to what is published on your own site. At each question the chatbot looks up the most relevant excerpts and gives them to the AI model together with your instructions. If it does not find the answer, you can tell it to say so instead of guessing.

Where can I place the chatbot?

As a floating widget on the whole site or only on selected pages, or inside any page with the [botshido] shortcode. The shortcode works wherever your editor or page builder accepts shortcodes.

Is visitor data stored?

Conversations and analytics events with minimized data are stored in your WordPress database, with configurable retention periods. The plugin integrates with the WordPress privacy tools (data export and erasure).

Does Botshido support GDPR requirements?

Botshido includes the tools you need to run a chatbot in line with GDPR: an optional consent notice that blocks the chat (and analytics) until the visitor accepts, configurable data retention, conversations kept in your own database, and integration with the WordPress personal data export and erase tools for conversations and analytics. Compliance also depends on your privacy policy and on the agreement you have with your AI provider, so this is not legal advice.

Does Botshido help with the EU AI Act?

It helps you tell visitors that they are talking to an AI: the bundled chatbots greet with a sentence that says so, the admin suggests an unambiguous bot name and warns you when no opening message exists, and an AI Disclaimer link in the chat footer gives the full text. How you configure and word it remains your responsibility, and this is not legal advice. The free checklist and a privacy notice template are at https://botshido.com/docs/.

What happens to a visitor who declines the consent notice?

With the consent notice enabled, nothing is sent to the AI provider and no conversation or analytics data is recorded for that visitor.

Can it hand a conversation over to a person?

Human handoff, with availability hours and operator notifications, is part of Botshido Pro.

Can I run more than one chatbot?

The free plugin runs one chatbot. Botshido Pro lets you create as many as you need, each with its own configuration, provider settings and appearance.

What do templates include?

Free includes Ninji, Leo and Aria with their prompts, colors and avatars. Applying a template replaces its supported prompt and appearance fields; it preserves API keys, knowledge and conversations. Undo restores the last application. Updating the plugin does not automatically reapply templates.

You can import a template file (ZIP, with images) in the free plugin. Botshido Pro adds the online template library, template export and creating chatbots from templates. JSON imports do not transfer images. ZIP requires the PHP ZIP extension.
sections.changelog:
1.2.8

  • The chatbot now knows the address of the pages and posts it retrieves from the knowledge base and can link to them when it helps the visitor. No reindexing is needed and links follow slug changes. Only published content without a password is linked.
  • Fixed: selecting specific pages or posts in the knowledge base no longer excludes the other checked content types. The selection now concerns pages and posts only, and selected items are indexed even if the Page or Post type is unchecked; every other checked type is indexed in full at the next re-index, so uncheck the types you do not want.
  • Fixed: after accepting the privacy notice the message field stayed locked until the closing animation ended, so a question typed right away could be lost. It is now unlocked immediately.
  • Fixed: reopening the chat after moving to another page showed the start of the conversation instead of the latest message.
  • The opening bubble no longer reappears once the visitor has written to the chatbot, or after the visitor closes it with the X (until the end of the browser session). It also no longer pops up right after the chat is closed.
  • Fixed: the base prompt and training text limits counted bytes instead of characters, so a long text with accents could be refused and lost on save. Characters are now counted, and a text over the limit stays on the page with a message.
  • The Chatbots list has an on/off switch in the Status column to show or hide each chatbot on the site without opening its settings. It changes the same setting as Display & Placement.
  • Pro: exported template ZIP files are named after the chatbot, for example framboisine-template.zip.

1.2.7

  • Fixed: on sites with a page cache (LiteSpeed, WP Rocket, Cloudflare and similar) the chat could stop working for logged-out visitors once the cached page was more than a day old, answering every message with an error. The widget now fetches a fresh security token when the cached one has expired and retries the request automatically.
  • Usage limits, in Settings → API under “Usage limits (all chatbots)”: the daily limit of AI requests for the whole site can now be changed from the panel, which also shows how many requests were used today. Each visitor can send at most 15 messages per minute, 100 per hour and 400 per day by default; the three limits are adjustable, 0 turns a limit off, and administrators are never limited.
  • Email alerts: the site administrator receives an email when 80% of the daily limit is used and when the limit is reached, at most once per level per day. They can be turned off.
  • When the daily limit is reached, the chat shows a message you choose and keeps offering the quick questions linked to a content block, which do not use the AI, together with the button to talk to a person.
  • A chat session now sends one AI request at a time, so repeated clicks or scripts cannot multiply the cost of a single conversation.
  • The panel warns when the site seems to run behind a proxy or CDN without trusted proxy ranges configured, because all visitors could then share the same per-visitor limit.
  • Botshido now requires PHP 8.1 or later. Sites on an older PHP version keep the version they have; WordPress will offer the update once PHP is upgraded.

1.2.6

  • AI transparency: the chat footer link is now called “AI Disclaimer” and its text starts with an explicit statement that the visitor is talking to an AI; label and text are translatable per chatbot (WPML/Polylang). The bundled chatbots and new chatbots greet with a sentence that says they are an AI assistant, and the admin suggests an unambiguous bot name and warns when no opening message exists.
  • The system prompt now always tells the assistant to state that it is an AI when asked whether it is a human; this instruction cannot be removed from the base prompt.
  • The bundled chatbots Ninji, Leo and Aria have new, structured base prompts: role, audience, objectives, tone, answer length and mandatory rules (answer only from the knowledge base, no invented data, no sensitive data, never promise a human follow-up that cannot happen). Colors, avatars and names are unchanged. Existing chatbots keep their prompts until the template is applied again.
  • A discreet request for a review on WordPress.org: shown only to administrators of the free plugin, only on Botshido screens, after two weeks of use and at least 10 conversations. It can be postponed or dismissed for good, and nothing is offered or locked in exchange.
  • The Settings API tab and the setup wizard link to the step-by-step guide for getting an API key and understanding the costs.
  • Documentation: a Documentation link in the Plugins list and in the Botshido menu, opening https://botshido.com/docs/ (Italian: /docs/it/ when the administrator’s language is Italian).
  • OpenAI models: the list now offers GPT-6.1 (Sol, Terra) next to GPT-6 and GPT-5.6, and the default for new chatbots is gpt-6-luna. GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini are no longer offered because OpenAI is retiring them; chatbots that still use them switch to a current model automatically once OpenAI stops serving them.
  • Claude and Mistral models: the lists now offer Claude Haiku 5.5 (a fast, low-cost option) and Claude Fable 5.2, and Mistral Large 4. The retired or retiring Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Fable 5.1, Mistral Medium 3.5 and Mistral Large 3 are no longer offered. Saved choices are kept.
  • Fixed: chatting in two browser tabs of the same site no longer locks the first tab out with “Conversation access denied”. The session cookie now authorizes the most recent sessions of the browser, and if the server still cannot recognise a session (for example when cookies are blocked or were cleared) the chat continues in a new session instead of stopping.
  • Pro: custom intents now work. A new field in the Base Prompt tab accepts up to 10 intents as “name: description”; the description teaches the AI when to pick your intent, the new intents appear in the Intent trigger list of the content blocks editor, and blocks triggered by them fire with every supported provider.

1.2.5

  • First public release.
